review_notes: I read the whole file and checked each new definition against Mathlib concepts. The definitions are SpliceState, exchangeState, undoState, ValidSpliceStep, SpliceExecution, undoExecution, separatingBonds, bridgeIndex, bridgeInterval, ordinalSpliceCode, domainBits, spliceTupleWeight, traceHeadGap, gapSpliceCode, decodeGapOrdinals, gapWeight, inverseCodeMass, gapLetterWeight and contactInterval. Each is either a domain-specific percolation notion or a thin named wrapper over a Mathlib operation: Finset.filter, Set.Finite.toFinset, a product type, Function.update, and a list recursion. A named wrapper is not a defect under the rubric. contactInterval is definitionally Set.Ico on unitInterval, but it is stated with real inequalities and is used directly in the product-measure computation. I judged it a convenience definition, not a competing concept. A few standalone lemmas, such as sum_fin_succ_eq_Icc, partly restate Mathlib facts. The rubric excludes standalone theorem duplication, so I did not report them. I did not open Geometry.lean to compare exchangeOn or finiteExchange against Mathlib, because those are defined outside this file. I found no justified finding.
